office_does: The sheriff runs the Asotin County Sheriff's Office, the county's chief law-enforcement agency, which patrols, investigates, serves court process and warrants, and leads the newly opened county jail.
race_blurb: Open seat: Sheriff John Hilderbrand is not on the ballot. Undersheriff Blake Richards, a Pullman fire captain and former Life Flight base manager who moved into full-time law enforcement in recent years, faces City of Asotin Police Chief Monte Renzelman, a 31-year Lewis-Clark Valley officer. Richards led the primary 50.7% to 49.0%; both oppose the state's new sheriff-qualification law, which a judge has paused.

candidates.summary: Asotin County undersheriff since July 2025, a full-time Pullman firefighter-paramedic captain and former Life Flight Lewiston base manager, running on putting criminals in jail and better equipping deputies.
highlights: Undersheriff since July 2025; reserve officer since 2011, then an emergency hire and patrol deputy [S1][S3][S5]
Would work through more than 1,500 outstanding warrants and target drug dealers: 'criminals should be in jail' [S2][S4]
Wants patrol rifles and modern equipment issued to deputies, plus regular town halls [S2]

safety.basis: Repeated, explicit enforcement framing: Washington 'making excuses for criminals', 'criminals should be in jail', clearing 1,500 warrants, targeting drug dealers and building strong cases with the prosecutor; no prevention or treatment plank.

experience.basis: Mixed profile: he is the current administration's undersheriff, but came to full-time law enforcement only in recent years after a fire, paramedic and air-medical career, and runs on new practices (issued rifles, town halls, in-house instructors).

candidates.summary: City of Asotin police chief for 11 years and a 31-year Lewis-Clark Valley officer, including as a county deputy sergeant, running on experience, fentanyl enforcement and jail reentry programs.
highlights: Asotin police chief for 11 years; earlier 13 years with Lewiston police and a deputy sergeant with the Sheriff's Office [S2]
Would 'aggressively confront the fentanyl epidemic' through enforcement, prevention and education [S1]
Supports jail treatment, education, job training and structured release to reduce reoffending [S1][S2]
Endorsed by former Asotin County Sheriffs John Jeffers and Wayne Weber [S3]

experience.basis: Runs on a long proven record ('Experience You Can Trust'): 31 years in the valley's departments, more than 10 as a chief, endorsed by two former sheriffs; not the incumbent in this office.

safety.basis: Leads with drug-supply enforcement and task-force work but pairs it with treatment, reentry programs, structured release and community policing, and set up a fund to help people in crisis.
